world.title: Russia-Ukraine truce holds in Oleshky as aid corridor preparations advance
world.summary: A six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine remained in effect Wednesday, with Russian and Ukrainian human rights officials reporting no violations in its first 30 hours. The truce began Oct. 27 and is scheduled to last through Nov. 1. About 2,000 people remain in Oleshky, where residents ha
world.content: A six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine remained in effect Wednesday, with Russian and Ukrainian human rights officials reporting no violations in its first 30 hours. The truce began Oct. 27 and is scheduled to last through Nov. 1. About 2,000 people remain in Oleshky, where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. Ukrainian officials said crews were clearing mines from an aid delivery route. Doctors, medicines, food and water are to be sent before evacuation corridors open. Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said officials from Ukraine, Russia and the United States would be present after the road is cleared and aid arrives. The pause has also brought a temporary lull in attacks on nearby Kherson, while fighting continues elsewhere. Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. delegations are discussing another U.S.-brokered meeting in Abu Dhabi in November, but no date has been set.
world.image_alt: Russia-Ukraine truce holds in Oleshky as aid corridor preparations advance

world.title: North Korea fires about a dozen missiles as border tensions rise
world.summary: North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from its east coast toward the sea on Thursday, South Korea’s military said. The missiles were launched from near Wonsan at about 12:30 p.m. and flew roughly 250 kilometers; South Korea and the United States were analyzing their specifications. Japan said the su
world.content: North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from its east coast toward the sea on Thursday, South Korea’s military said. The missiles were launched from near Wonsan at about 12:30 p.m. and flew roughly 250 kilometers; South Korea and the United States were analyzing their specifications. Japan said the suspected missile fell outside its exclusive economic zone. The launches followed landmine blasts near the border that injured three South Korean soldiers on Sept. 21. A joint investigation by South Korea and the United Nations said North Korea had planted the mines south of the military demarcation line more than a year earlier; Pyongyang denies responsibility. Seoul proposed military talks to clarify the border and restore communication channels, but North Korea has not responded. Pyongyang had also threatened to resume propaganda broadcasts and deploy weapons along the border. President Donald Trump has expressed interest in renewed diplomacy with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, prompting concern in Seoul that it could be excluded from any nuclear talks. South Korea said it was monitoring for further launches and sharing information with the United States and Japan.
world.image_alt: North Korea fires about a dozen missiles as border tensions rise

world.title: Putin pitches African partnership as Moscow seeks trade, security ties
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin used the Oct. 28-29 Russia-Africa summit in Moscow to cast Russia as Africa’s best partner, accusing Western countries of exploiting the continent and using debt to constrain development. Delegations from 48 African countries attended, including 22 leaders, for talks on trade, security,
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin used the Oct. 28-29 Russia-Africa summit in Moscow to cast Russia as Africa’s best partner, accusing Western countries of exploiting the continent and using debt to constrain development. Delegations from 48 African countries attended, including 22 leaders, for talks on trade, security, arms and grain. The Kremlin is seeking wider political, economic and military influence as it faces Western pressure over its war in Ukraine. Putin offered expanded grain and fertilizer supplies, local production and technology sharing, joint transport and agricultural infrastructure, and greater African influence at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. He said Russia had shipped 13 million metric tonnes of agricultural products to Africa during the first nine months of 2026 and called for Russia-Africa trade to more than double to above $50 billion from over $27 billion last year. The summit’s second day was scheduled to produce a partnership declaration, an artificial-intelligence cooperation statement and a 2027-2029 action plan, alongside 33 agreements. Human-rights advocates urged African leaders to confront Russia over deceptive or coercive recruitment of Africans to fight in Ukraine. Experts also questioned whether Moscow has the money to deliver on its broader economic ambitions.
world.image_alt: Putin pitches African partnership as Moscow seeks trade, security ties

world.title: Kremlin says Ukraine talks will resume after Nov. 4, without Europe
world.summary: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia, Ukraine and the United States will resume trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi after Nov. 4, but Moscow has not set a date. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he hopes negotiators can meet between Nov. 6 and 10, after the U.S. midterm elections. President Dona
world.content: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia, Ukraine and the United States will resume trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi after Nov. 4, but Moscow has not set a date. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he hopes negotiators can meet between Nov. 6 and 10, after the U.S. midterm elections. President Donald Trump separately said a face-to-face meeting between Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin would be arranged “very soon,” without giving details. Ushakov said the timing could depend on battlefield conditions and the wider situation, including the war in the Middle East. European negotiators would not take part, he said, describing the agreed format as consultations among Russia, Ukraine and the United States. Kyiv wants Europe involved in efforts to end the war, while Washington has led the latest diplomatic push. Zelensky said the meeting date would be settled after the Nov. 3 U.S. elections. Ushakov said the date would be announced soon but did not specify when.
world.image_alt: Kremlin says Ukraine talks will resume after Nov. 4, without Europe

world.title: EU and Canada drop associate-member label, set 2027 partnership talks
world.summary: The European Union and Canada have dropped the proposed “associate member” status from a summit declaration, opting instead to define an “ever closer association” by their 2027 summit. EU member states approved the revised wording ahead of a two-day meeting in Montreal hosted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The
world.content: The European Union and Canada have dropped the proposed “associate member” status from a summit declaration, opting instead to define an “ever closer association” by their 2027 summit. EU member states approved the revised wording ahead of a two-day meeting in Montreal hosted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The declaration is expected to be published Friday, Oct. 30. The change follows objections led by Germany, with France and other governments also opposing a label that has no basis in EU treaties and could blur the distinction between Canada and countries seeking EU accession. Canada has no intention of joining the bloc, Carney has said. He is pursuing closer European ties as President Donald Trump’s tariffs and threats have pushed Ottawa to reduce its economic and security dependence on the United States. The summit declaration is expected to advance cooperation on digital trade, critical minerals, energy, defense and secure communications, including plans for subsea cables linking Europe, Canada and Asia. The sides are also discussing a study of Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe. Formal talks to define their relationship are to continue through next year.
world.image_alt: EU and Canada drop associate-member label, set 2027 partnership talks

world.title: Manhattan judge Alvin Hellerstein dies, leaving Maduro trial to successor
world.summary: U.S. District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein, who was overseeing the federal prosecution of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, died Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 92. The court reassigned the case to U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres, according to a court filing. Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, face narco-terrorism and d
world.content: U.S. District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein, who was overseeing the federal prosecution of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, died Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 92. The court reassigned the case to U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres, according to a court filing. Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, face narco-terrorism and drug-trafficking charges, as well as newer torture-related charges. Hellerstein presided over their arraignment about two weeks before his death; the trial is scheduled for June 2027. Hellerstein also repeatedly rejected President Donald Trump’s attempts to move his New York hush-money case to federal court. In August, he again ruled against Trump after an appeals court directed him to reconsider the immunity arguments. Lawyer and former federal prosecutor Duncan Levin said Hellerstein’s death does not automatically pause the Maduro case; Torres can keep or adjust the schedule.
world.image_alt: Manhattan judge Alvin Hellerstein dies, leaving Maduro trial to successor

world.title: Vance contacts Iran security chief as Trump weighs renewed strikes
world.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, seeking to reopen talks as President Donald Trump weighs renewed military action against Iran. The Wall Street Journal reported that the outreach tested whether the two sides could establish a negotiating
world.content: U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, seeking to reopen talks as President Donald Trump weighs renewed military action against Iran. The Wall Street Journal reported that the outreach tested whether the two sides could establish a negotiating framework; The New York Times said Vance proposed resuming comprehensive talks, including on Iran’s nuclear program. Trump acknowledged approving Vance’s contact but denied directing him to restart peace negotiations, saying the outreach concerned medical supplies. He has not made a final decision on new strikes, which Washington has discussed carrying out after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remained in contact with mediators over a seven-day plan to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. If Iran accepts the proposal, talks could begin as early as next week in Qatar or Turkey, according to officials cited by The New York Times.
world.image_alt: Vance contacts Iran security chief as Trump weighs renewed strikes

world.title: Putin praises Musk as Russia builds satellite network for military use
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised SpaceX founder Elon Musk on Wednesday and said Russia was in close contact with him as Moscow builds Rassvet, a satellite internet network intended to rival SpaceX’s Starlink for civilian and military use. Russia has launched more than 30 satellites, Digital Development Minister
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised SpaceX founder Elon Musk on Wednesday and said Russia was in close contact with him as Moscow builds Rassvet, a satellite internet network intended to rival SpaceX’s Starlink for civilian and military use. Russia has launched more than 30 satellites, Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadayev said. Putin described the effort as an early step and said Russia must expand its constellation. The remarks followed Ukraine’s reports of service restrictions on Starlink and its military-focused counterpart, Starshield, which Ukrainian forces rely on for battlefield communications, drone operations and air defenses. Ukraine said the slowdown hampered efforts to intercept Russian drones and disrupted some operations. Kyiv announced on Oct. 24 that both services had been restored. Musk said SpaceX had closed a loophole after Ukraine used civilian Starlink for offensive drone strikes, while neither he nor the U.S. government accepted responsibility for the earlier speed restrictions. Russia plans to expand Rassvet to 292 satellites by the end of 2027 and about 900 by 2035.
world.image_alt: Putin praises Musk as Russia builds satellite network for military use

business.title: Weil Gotshal recommends dissolution after partner exodus and merger failure
business.summary: Leaders of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, a nearly century-old U.S. law firm, recommended dissolving the firm after a wave of senior lawyer departures and failed merger talks. Partners are expected to vote on the proposal in the coming days. The firm says it will continue serving clients during an orderly wind-down over the c
business.content: Leaders of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, a nearly century-old U.S. law firm, recommended dissolving the firm after a wave of senior lawyer departures and failed merger talks. Partners are expected to vote on the proposal in the coming days. The firm says it will continue serving clients during an orderly wind-down over the coming months. The firm had about 1,200 lawyers, roughly 1,000 other staff and about $2 billion in revenue last year, with little or no debt, but still faces office leases and pension obligations. Its leadership has hired restructuring adviser AlixPartners and is working with Davis Polk & Wardwell on the process. The departures included teams serving major private-equity clients. The firm also failed to secure a proposed combination with Willkie Farr & Gallagher.
business.image_alt: Weil Gotshal recommends dissolution after partner exodus and merger failure

business.title: Canada, EU conclude digital trade talks, agree on critical-minerals investment deal
business.summary: Canada and the European Union have concluded substantive negotiations on a digital trade agreement, according to a draft statement prepared for their Montreal summit. The proposed rules would cover cross-border data flows, e-signatures, e-contracts and paperless trade, with the aim of giving businesses and consumers gr
business.content: Canada and the European Union have concluded substantive negotiations on a digital trade agreement, according to a draft statement prepared for their Montreal summit. The proposed rules would cover cross-border data flows, e-signatures, e-contracts and paperless trade, with the aim of giving businesses and consumers greater legal certainty in online commerce. The draft also proposes linking Canadian and European instant-payment systems to make cross-border transfers faster and cheaper. The two sides are pursuing closer economic ties under a revised “ever closer association” formula, with the summit declaration expected Friday, Oct. 30. The EU bought about $43 billion in Canadian goods in 2025, while it imported more than $700 billion in product categories where Canadian exporters may be competitive, according to TD Economics. The bank said infrastructure and other barriers must be addressed to expand trade.
business.image_alt: Canada, EU conclude digital trade talks, agree on critical-minerals investment deal

business.title: US health chief eases restrictions on compounding six unapproved peptides
business.summary: U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. issued a policy on Oct. 28 directing the department not to enforce certain rules against licensed pharmacies and physicians who compound six unapproved peptides: BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and TB-500. The policy does not grant Food and Drug
business.content: U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. issued a policy on Oct. 28 directing the department not to enforce certain rules against licensed pharmacies and physicians who compound six unapproved peptides: BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and TB-500. The policy does not grant Food and Drug Administration approval or establish that the substances are safe or effective. It sets conditions including patient-specific prescriptions, traceable ingredients, quality testing and safety reporting. The move follows a July FDA advisory panel recommendation to allow the peptides, despite FDA staff objections that evidence of their safety and effectiveness is insufficient. The policy is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Oct. 30, with public comments accepted through Nov. 13. It remains in place until the FDA finalizes a rule on compounded peptides, which the agency has not yet proposed.
business.image_alt: US health chief eases restrictions on compounding six unapproved peptides

business.title: Utah charges Kalshi and founders with 14 gambling counts
business.summary: Utah filed 14 criminal charges against prediction-market operator Kalshi and its co-founders, Chief Executive Tarek Mansour and Chief Operating Officer Luana Lopes Lara, accusing them of promoting illegal gambling. The case includes 12 felony counts tied to online gambling promotion, one felony alleging a pattern of un
business.content: Utah filed 14 criminal charges against prediction-market operator Kalshi and its co-founders, Chief Executive Tarek Mansour and Chief Operating Officer Luana Lopes Lara, accusing them of promoting illegal gambling. The case includes 12 felony counts tied to online gambling promotion, one felony alleging a pattern of unlawful activity and one misdemeanor count. Prosecutors say an undercover state investigator placed 12 sports wagers on Kalshi; the charges follow Utah’s civil lawsuit seeking to stop the company’s operations in the state. Utah and Kalshi dispute whether the company’s event contracts fall under state gambling laws or the federal oversight of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the U.S. derivatives regulator. A federal judge ruled in August that Utah could enforce its gambling laws against Kalshi, while the commission sued Utah on Oct. 27, arguing federal law gives it exclusive authority over the markets. Kalshi called the charges a “crazy overreach” and said it would fight them in court.
business.image_alt: Utah charges Kalshi and founders with 14 gambling counts

business.title: Oracle caps AI fundraising at $20 billion, targets $30 billion cash flow
business.summary: Oracle shares climbed more than 12% on Wednesday after the enterprise software company told investors it expects more than $30 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2029 and will cap additional AI-related fundraising at $20 billion through fiscal 2030. Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said the funding would be split
business.content: Oracle shares climbed more than 12% on Wednesday after the enterprise software company told investors it expects more than $30 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2029 and will cap additional AI-related fundraising at $20 billion through fiscal 2030. Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said the funding would be split equally between debt and equity. Oracle expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028. Oracle is expanding its data centers as it competes to sell computing capacity to AI customers. The company also maintained its fiscal 2030 revenue target of more than $225 billion and said it expects to deliver seven gigawatts of data-center capacity over the next couple of years. Oracle has said vendor financing, customer-supplied hardware and prepayments will help reduce cash needs before the business generates positive free cash flow.
business.image_alt: Oracle caps AI fundraising at $20 billion, targets $30 billion cash flow

business.title: Activist investor Nelson Peltz offers $1.4 billion to take Wendy’s private
business.summary: A group led by activist investor Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management offered $7.35 a share in cash, or about $1.4 billion, to buy burger chain Wendy’s and take it private. The unsolicited, nonbinding offer represents a premium of nearly 20% to the stock’s Tuesday closing price; Trian and affiliated investors own about
business.content: A group led by activist investor Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management offered $7.35 a share in cash, or about $1.4 billion, to buy burger chain Wendy’s and take it private. The unsolicited, nonbinding offer represents a premium of nearly 20% to the stock’s Tuesday closing price; Trian and affiliated investors own about 16.3% of Wendy’s. The consortium also includes BlueFive Capital, Sixth Street Partners and Flynn Group, a large Wendy’s franchisee. Wendy’s said its independent board committee will review the proposal; the company’s shares rose about 15% after the offer became public. The chain faces higher food costs, weaker consumer traffic and competition while working to refresh its menu and improve restaurant operations. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter results on Nov. 5, when it also expects to discuss its strategic plan.
business.image_alt: Activist investor Nelson Peltz offers $1.4 billion to take Wendy’s private

business.title: SK Hynix secures customer deals covering half of 2027-28 chip output
business.summary: SK Hynix said long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than half of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028. The South Korean memory-chip maker reported third-quarter revenue of 104.61 trillion won and operating profit of 83.33 trillion won. The deals reserve supply years in advance, typically run for
business.content: SK Hynix said long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than half of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028. The South Korean memory-chip maker reported third-quarter revenue of 104.61 trillion won and operating profit of 83.33 trillion won. The deals reserve supply years in advance, typically run for five years, allow prices to move within agreed ranges and include safeguards such as customer deposits. The company said its DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production was sold out through 2029 and forecast memory shortages through 2030 as AI infrastructure spending drives demand. Executives said demand is spreading beyond major cloud companies to non-tech businesses and government-backed AI projects. The company cited cloud customers’ year-over-year revenue growth of 30% to 80% and order backlogs two to five times higher. SK Hynix also announced a further 60 trillion won in buybacks and dividends after completing a 40 trillion-won shareholder-return program. Net profit fell 57.7% from the previous quarter to 39.78 trillion won, partly because the prior quarter benefited from a rise in the share price of Kioxia, a Japanese memory-chip maker in which SK Hynix holds a stake.
business.image_alt: SK Hynix secures customer deals covering half of 2027-28 chip output

business.title: Jio shares rise 5% as debut boosts India’s IPO pipeline
business.summary: Shares in Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital-services business of Reliance Industries, climbed as much as 5% to 1,490 rupees in early trading on Thursday, their second session after listing in India’s largest-ever IPO. At that high, the stock was about 33% above its 1,119-rupee offer price; it later retreated from
business.content: Shares in Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital-services business of Reliance Industries, climbed as much as 5% to 1,490 rupees in early trading on Thursday, their second session after listing in India’s largest-ever IPO. At that high, the stock was about 33% above its 1,119-rupee offer price; it later retreated from the session’s peak, according to live market updates. Brokerage Elara Securities estimated digital services would account for 12% of Jio’s revenue in the current financial year, while analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services said Jio had yet to demonstrate it could monetize newer services at scale. On listing day, Motilal Oswal and Elara set target prices of 1,350 and 1,367 rupees, respectively, both below Thursday’s intraday high. In India’s IPO pipeline, 113 companies have regulatory approval to list and 115 have filed draft papers. Possible offerings include PhonePe, Flipkart, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages and Tata Sons. Indian IPOs have raised $18.26 billion so far this year, compared with last year’s record $22.36 billion.
business.image_alt: Jio shares rise 5% as debut boosts India’s IPO pipeline

science.title: Forecasts point to record-early polar vortex split in November
science.summary: Forecasts published Oct. 28 indicate that stratospheric winds could reverse in early November and split the northern polar vortex, potentially producing the earliest sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) event on record, at least three weeks earlier than the previous benchmark. The event is forecast, not confirmed. Models
science.content: Forecasts published Oct. 28 indicate that stratospheric winds could reverse in early November and split the northern polar vortex, potentially producing the earliest sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) event on record, at least three weeks earlier than the previous benchmark. The event is forecast, not confirmed. Models signal possible cooling in parts of Europe, Finland and the eastern United States, but a disrupted vortex does not guarantee cold weather in any particular region. Atmospheric conditions are still transitioning into winter, and the strength of any surface effects depends on how the stratospheric change interacts with lower-level circulation. Forecasts indicate a possible wind reversal around Nov. 4, and ECMWF forecasts show below-normal temperatures in parts of Europe around Nov. 8.
science.image_alt: Forecasts point to record-early polar vortex split in November

science.title: Researchers map immune-cell surfaces and image activity deep in mouse brains
science.summary: Researchers mapped proteins on the surfaces of human T lymphocytes and B lymphoblasts, identifying established and previously unrecognized protein groupings, including mitochondrial proteins at the cell membrane. The study also linked the IL-10 receptor beta subunit to regulation of type I interferon signaling. Separat
science.content: Researchers mapped proteins on the surfaces of human T lymphocytes and B lymphoblasts, identifying established and previously unrecognized protein groupings, including mitochondrial proteins at the cell membrane. The study also linked the IL-10 receptor beta subunit to regulation of type I interferon signaling. Separately, a Rockefeller University team used its Three-photon Ultra-Deep Imaging platform to record neuronal activity as deep as 2.1 millimeters in intact mouse brains. In an interview, computational biologist Christina Leslie of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center said current AI models still cannot reliably predict how cells will respond to untested drugs or genetic changes.

science.title: Cyclone Arnab batters India
science.summary: Cyclone Arnab made landfall along India’s Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast early Oct. 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 125-135 kph and gusts up to 150 kph, before weakening inland. India’s National Disaster Response Force initially reported three deaths and damage to 31 houses in Andhra Pradesh
science.content: Cyclone Arnab made landfall along India’s Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast early Oct. 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 125-135 kph and gusts up to 150 kph, before weakening inland. India’s National Disaster Response Force initially reported three deaths and damage to 31 houses in Andhra Pradesh; NDTV later reported five deaths in separate incidents. Heavy rain remained a threat inland as the storm weakened. Authorities said the cyclone inundated about 200,000 acres of cropland, while damage to homes and infrastructure disrupted power and transport. Meteorologists said unusually warm Bay of Bengal waters helped fuel Arnab and its rapid intensification. Experts said human-caused warming can amplify cyclone rainfall but did not attribute this storm solely to climate change. NASA said Arnab was the first named storm of the 2026 North Indian Ocean season. It emerged on Oct. 25, later than the basin’s typical April or May start.

science.title: Webb maps young stars in Large Magellanic Cloud nursery
science.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured an image of N159, a star-forming complex in the Large Magellanic Cloud about 161,000 light-years from Earth, revealing dense gas filaments and thousands of young stars. The region spans about 230 light-years and is less than 3 million years old. Researchers distinguished star
science.content: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured an image of N159, a star-forming complex in the Large Magellanic Cloud about 161,000 light-years from Earth, revealing dense gas filaments and thousands of young stars. The region spans about 230 light-years and is less than 3 million years old. Researchers distinguished stars still embedded in their birth clouds from older populations, including very faint stars with less than one-tenth the Sun’s mass. They found a denser concentration of young stellar objects in N159’s western portion than in the east, a pattern they said suggests star formation is at an earlier stage in the west. The research paper was posted on arXiv on Sept. 22, 2026.
science.image_alt: Webb maps young stars in Large Magellanic Cloud nursery

science.title: Caltech study finds Eaton Fire smoke exposed 7 million to lead
science.summary: A Caltech-led study estimates that about 7 million people in the Los Angeles area were exposed to 24-hour lead concentrations more than 80 times typical levels during the peak burning of structures in the January 2025 Eaton Fire. Published Oct. 28 in Science Advances, the research compared real-time measurements of the
science.content: A Caltech-led study estimates that about 7 million people in the Los Angeles area were exposed to 24-hour lead concentrations more than 80 times typical levels during the peak burning of structures in the January 2025 Eaton Fire. Published Oct. 28 in Science Advances, the research compared real-time measurements of the Eaton plume with smoke from a fire that burned mostly vegetation in Riverside County. The Eaton plume contained more than 50 times as much lead, seven times as much chlorine and bromine, and about three times as much arsenic as the comparison wildfire plume. Researchers linked the difference to burning homes, vehicles and other urban materials. They said the health consequences of brief, intense exposure to these metals and chemical mixtures remain unknown and called for epidemiological studies, particularly involving children and other vulnerable groups.
science.image_alt: Caltech study finds Eaton Fire smoke exposed 7 million to lead

science.title: Trump EPA proposes loosening methane rules, ending leak-reporting program
science.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration proposed easing federal methane controls for oil and gas operations, including ending a program that uses approved outside monitors to flag major leaks. The rules cover existing facilities as well as new ones. Trump announced the proposal at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Oct. 27,
science.content: President Donald Trump’s administration proposed easing federal methane controls for oil and gas operations, including ending a program that uses approved outside monitors to flag major leaks. The rules cover existing facilities as well as new ones. Trump announced the proposal at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Oct. 27, describing the Biden-era rules as costly and unnecessary. The Environmental Protection Agency says the changes could save energy producers and consumers $45 billion and allow producers to extract an additional 210 million barrels of oil and 1.41 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. The agency has not provided a detailed breakdown of its savings estimate. Federal officials under the Biden administration projected that the 2024 rule would prevent 58 million tons of methane emissions through 2038. The changes remain a proposal, not a final rule. The EPA plans a public comment period of at least 45 days and a hearing after publication in the Federal Register.
science.image_alt: Trump EPA proposes loosening methane rules, ending leak-reporting program

science.title: HHS eases restrictions on peptide compounding despite gaps in human safety evidence
science.summary: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. directed the Food and Drug Administration not to enforce certain rules against licensed pharmacies and physicians compounding six unapproved peptides, despite objections from FDA scientists who say evidence of their safety and effectiveness remains inadequa
science.content: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. directed the Food and Drug Administration not to enforce certain rules against licensed pharmacies and physicians compounding six unapproved peptides, despite objections from FDA scientists who say evidence of their safety and effectiveness remains inadequate. The policy covers BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and TB-500; it does not give them FDA approval or establish that they are safe or effective. An FDA advisory panel recommended allowing pharmacies and physicians to compound the six peptides in July, but FDA staff advised against the move. The substances have little or no human research, and the FDA had previously cited possible risks including allergic reactions, kidney damage and tumor growth. HHS says pharmacies must use traceable ingredients, conduct quality testing and report safety problems. The notice is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Oct. 30, with comments accepted through Nov. 13.
science.image_alt: HHS eases restrictions on peptide compounding despite gaps in human safety evidence

science.title: Researchers identify new dinosaur genus from fossil found in England in 2001
science.summary: Paleontologists have classified a fossil found in a Surrey clay quarry in 2001 as Paludohadros proudlovii, a previously unknown genus and species of plant-eating dinosaur that lived about 125 million years ago. The four-legged animal was about 5 metres long and weighed an estimated 1.5 to 2 metric tons, but its bones i
science.content: Paleontologists have classified a fossil found in a Surrey clay quarry in 2001 as Paludohadros proudlovii, a previously unknown genus and species of plant-eating dinosaur that lived about 125 million years ago. The four-legged animal was about 5 metres long and weighed an estimated 1.5 to 2 metric tons, but its bones indicate it had not reached adulthood. The fossil was donated to London’s Natural History Museum, where it remained for years before a detailed comparison with other iguanodontians revealed distinguishing features. The identification also helped researchers identify fossils collected from the same quarry in the 1950s as belonging to the newly named dinosaur. The research, led by Ricardo Sacamoto, a PhD student at the Natural History Museum and the University of São Paulo, was published in the Journal of Systematic Palaeontology on Oct. 26, 2026. Sacamoto plans to continue examining the museum’s iguanodontian collection.
science.image_alt: Researchers identify new dinosaur genus from fossil found in England in 2001

sports.title: Colts receiver Josh Downs requests trade as Indianapolis reshapes roster
sports.summary: Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs requested a trade Wednesday, Oct. 28, one day after the 2-5 team traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. sports.content: Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs requested a trade Wednesday, Oct. 28, one day after the 2-5 team traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Downs, 25, leads Indianapolis with 26 receptions and 307 receiving yards in seven games and is in the final year of his rookie contract. Indianapolis is considering further roster moves. Coach Shane Steichen said running back Jonathan Taylor has not requested a trade. Downs has drawn interest from multiple AFC teams, including the Pittsburgh Steelers, although a deal was considered unlikely that week. Downs told reporters he is open to whatever happens. The Colts are scheduled to visit Jacksonville on Nov. 1 and host Dallas on Nov. 8, two days before the trade deadline.

sports.content: Prem Rugby and the Rugby Football Union (RFU) say English clubs remain their priority as they plan to expand the Gallagher Premiership, despite the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) exploring whether Welsh sides could join the league. The Premiership aims to grow from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season. The WRU says it will provide four teams to the United Rugby Championship (URC) through 2027-28 while it decides on a future model for Welsh men’s rugby. A Welsh move would require approval from both unions and an exit agreement with the URC; reports differ on how far discussions with English rugby have progressed. A tender for two new places is expected next month, and Welsh rugby’s future is due for discussion at a December summit.

The trade follows Seattle’s win over the Kansas City Chiefs, who are considering adding a receiver after injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton left them short of downfield targets. sports.content: Ernie Johnson will leave ESPN’s “Inside the NBA” after the 2026-27 season, ending a 37-year run as host of the basketball studio show. The 70-year-old broadcaster said the decision was his own. The extensive preparation that once brought him joy had become more difficult, and his heart problems and bypass surgery helped him reassess how he wants to spend his time. Johnson said he is not retiring from broadcasting. He plans to continue covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports and pursue other projects. He has also launched 32 Bowties, a production company focused on sports stories. “Inside the NBA” moved from TNT to ESPN and ABC in 2025, while TNT Sports continues to produce it. Fellow “Inside the NBA” analyst Charles Barkley has said he could leave if Johnson does, though he has reversed retirement plans before. ESPN and TNT Sports have not named a successor.

sports.content: Vincent Kompany, Bayern Munich’s 40-year-old head coach, was discharged from hospital on Wednesday, five days after collapsing while watching the club’s reserve team train. Sporting director Max Eberl said doctors identified meningeal irritation as the cause. Kompany had been ill with a virus and missed some training before he collapsed. He missed a news conference ahead of Bayern’s Champions League match against Arsenal but was on the touchline for the 2-2 draw. He is recovering at home with rest and medication. Assistant coach Aaron Danks has led Bayern in Kompany’s absence, overseeing a 3-1 league win at Freiburg and a 6-1 German Cup victory over Magdeburg. Bayern lead Borussia Dortmund on goal difference at the top of the Bundesliga, with the teams level on points. They meet in Munich on Saturday, October 31. The club has set no return date, and its doctors will decide when Kompany is fit to resume work.

sports.title: Real Madrid apologizes as China keeps La Liga broadcasts suspended
sports.summary: Real Madrid apologized to the Chinese people on Wednesday after forward Kylian Mbappé’s remarks about a meme depicting him as Mao Zedong prompted Chinese brands to end partnerships and state broadcaster China Media Group (CMG) to suspend Spanish league coverage. Mbappé had called the figure in the meme “a Chinese dicta
sports.content: Real Madrid apologized to the Chinese people on Wednesday after forward Kylian Mbappé’s remarks about a meme depicting him as Mao Zedong prompted Chinese brands to end partnerships and state broadcaster China Media Group (CMG) to suspend Spanish league coverage. Mbappé had called the figure in the meme “a Chinese dictator.” He issued a multilingual apology on Tuesday, and La Liga also expressed regret. China’s Foreign Ministry said it took Mbappé’s apology seriously, but CMG had rejected the club’s earlier explanation. Its broadcasts remained suspended after it received Real Madrid’s new statement. Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheese company Milkground canceled partnerships with Mbappé. Chinese platforms also restricted access to his accounts, while advertising featuring him was pulled. The clip came from a behind-the-scenes interview for the French show “The Bridge,” filmed months earlier and circulated online this week. The broadcaster has not announced when, or whether, Spanish league coverage will return. Sports commentator Yan Qiang told AFP that the apologies were unlikely to settle the matter quickly. La Liga president Javier Tebas has met China’s ambassador to Spain as the league works to contain the fallout.

sports.content: Swiss tennis player Stan Wawrinka ended his professional career on October 27 with a 7-5, 7-6(2) loss to Czech player Jiří Lehečka in the first round of the Swiss Indoors in Basel, his home tournament. The 41-year-old had announced that 2026 would be his final season, ending a career that began in 2002. Wawrinka won three Grand Slam singles titles, defeating Rafael Nadal in the 2014 Australian Open final and Novak Djokovic in the 2015 French Open and 2016 US Open finals. He was one of the few players to win multiple Grand Slam titles during an era dominated by Djokovic, Nadal and Roger Federer. He also won Olympic doubles gold with Federer in 2008 and helped Switzerland win its first Davis Cup in 2014. Wawrinka’s farewell season included a third-round run at the Australian Open and a brief return to the world’s top 100. A farewell exhibition in Geneva scheduled for December 19 will feature Federer and Andy Murray.

sports.content: Australia reached 330-4 at stumps on day two of the third Test in Cape Town, taking a one-run lead over South Africa’s 329 after Josh Inglis and Alex Carey added an unbeaten 145 for the fifth wicket. Inglis finished unbeaten on 85 and Carey on 51, leaving Australia with six wickets in hand in the series decider. The series is tied 1-1, and the winner of the match will take the No. 1 spot in the Test rankings, currently held by Australia. Australia built their reply without the injured Steve Smith, while Inglis returned after missing the first two Tests with a broken finger. Play resumes Thursday for day three.
